feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.

proposed_scope_in: Add a derived 'Recommended Contact' panel on the Country record that shows up to 3 contacts ranked by a deterministic rule: (1) contacts linked to an active Mission or Project for that Country, (2) most recent Engagement date, (3) contact record not flagged inactive
Show each recommended contact with role/title, ministry, preferred channel, last engagement date, and the linked Mission/Project that justified the ranking ('why this person')
Add a single optional boolean 'primary_for_country' flag on the existing Contact-Country link (no new table) that, if set, pins that contact to the top; otherwise ranking is fully automatic
Add 'last_verified' timestamp on Contact, auto-updated whenever an Engagement is logged against that contact, with a visible 'stale' badge if older than 12 months
Filter on the panel by topic via existing Project/Mission affiliation (e.g., 'contact for Mission X in Country Y') using existing links only
Search from the Country page and global search: 'who do I contact in [Country] for [Project/Mission]' returning the same ranked list
Respect existing Country/Mission record-level access: users only see contacts they can already see today
proposed_scope_out: No new Contact, Role, or Relationship tables and no multi-table historical role graph
No manual coordinator data-entry workflows, verification tasks, or approval chains
No ML or tunable scoring model; ranking is a fixed, documented, deterministic rule
No custom RBAC or new permission model; no new data classification or sensitivity tiers
No automated outreach, email/calendar integration, or contact-detail sync from external directories
No handling of diplomatic protocol, precedence, or seniority rules (a policy decision for humans, not product)
No bulk import/cleanup of existing contact data; v1 uses data as it exists
No UI configuration screens for ranking weights or rules
No cross-country or regional rollups of recommended contacts

assumptions.statement: 'Right person' means the best current point of contact for a given country, optionally scoped by Mission or Project, not a single universal contact per country.
assumptions.rationale: Scoping by existing Mission/Project links lets us answer the real question with data already in the CRM, avoiding a new 'contact role' taxonomy.

assumptions.statement: Existing data (Contact–Country, Contact–Mission, Contact–Project links and Engagement history) is good enough to derive a useful recommendation without cleanup.
assumptions.rationale: Deriving from Engagement history means zero new data entry for Regional Coordinators; recommendations improve automatically as they log work they already do.

assumptions.statement: Recency of engagement and active Mission/Project linkage are acceptable proxies for 'right person' in v1.
assumptions.rationale: A fixed, explainable rule is shippable in one cycle and easy to audit; a learned or tunable model would add cost and opacity.

assumptions.statement: Primary users are Operations and Country Engagement staff who already have access to the relevant Country/Mission records; no new access rules are needed.
assumptions.rationale: Inheriting existing record-level permissions avoids a custom RBAC build and prevents exposing contacts to people who could not see them before.

assumptions.statement: Contact position changes (a person leaving a role) are not detected automatically in v1; staleness is surfaced via a badge, not resolved.
assumptions.rationale: Detecting turnover requires external data or manual workflows; a stale badge gives an honest signal at zero coordinator effort.

assumptions.statement: Whether a given person is appropriate to contact for a sensitive topic is a diplomatic/policy judgment outside the CRM's remit.
assumptions.rationale: Keeping v1 to a decision-support list, rather than an authoritative routing engine, avoids inventing policy and keeps scope small.

success_criteria: Recommended Contact panel renders on 100% of Country records that have at least one linked Contact, with p95 load time under 2 seconds

In a pilot with at least 10 Operations/Country Engagement users, at least 80% say in a 3-question survey that the top-3 list contained the person they would have contacted for 10 sampled country lookups
Median time to find a point of contact for a given Country+Mission drops from the current baseline (measured pre-release on 10 timed tasks) by at least 50%
Zero new required fields for Regional Coordinators; no increase in coordinator data-entry time measured by form field count (0 new required fields)
100% of displayed recommendations show a 'why this person' justification and a last-engagement date or an explicit 'no engagement recorded' label
Zero instances in UAT of a user seeing a contact they cannot already access via existing Country/Mission permissions

challenges.challenge_text: Ranking by most recent Engagement date and active Mission linkage will surface people who have left their post. Example: a ministry liaison who attended three recent meetings resigns after a cabinet reshuffle. Nobody has logged a new engagement with the replacement, so the departed person stays ranked #1 with a fresh-looking 'why this person' justification. Staff then send sensitive correspondence to a former official. Because last_verified is only updated by logging an Engagement, it also marks a departed person as recently verified. It measures activity, not whether the person still holds the role. Also, no cleanup of inactive flags or duplicate contacts is planned, so data quality across 100 countries is unproven.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer admits in A5 that turnover is not detected and offers only a stale badge. The 12-month threshold is far too long for ministerial turnover. The ranking also presents confident 'why this person' output on data that may be wrong.

challenges.challenge_text: Inheriting existing Country/Mission record-level access is not enough once contacts are aggregated into a derived panel, global search, and a 'who do I contact' query. Today a user may see a Country record without being able to browse its contacts, or may see a Mission without seeing every contact linked to it. A new ranked cross-record view, and the justification text (Mission/Project names, last engagement dates), can expose the existence of confidential missions or engagement history to staff who lack access to the underlying Mission or Engagement. Global search is the highest-risk path because it is often built on an index that bypasses record-level filters. A coordinator who can see Country X but not a confidential Mission Y could infer Y's existence and the named contact from the 'why this person' line. The 'zero instances in UAT' criterion cannot verify this unless it explicitly tests the derived panel, search index, and justification strings.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer asserts that permissions are inherited but does not say how the derived panel, the search index, and the justification text enforce per-record and per-field access.

challenges.challenge_text: The Proposer treats recency of engagement as a proxy for the 'right' contact. In practice the most-engaged contact is often a junior desk officer or an administrative assistant, while the decision-maker is engaged rarely. Rule (1) also lets any contact linked to an active Mission outrank everyone else, even if the link is stale (a Mission closed on paper but still marked active). A coordinator following the top-3 list for an urgent or sensitive matter reaches the wrong level and may bypass the correct ministry channel, a diplomatic misstep. There is also no handling of ties, contacts with no engagement history, or a country with more than three valid contacts. The 80% survey criterion is weak: it measures agreement with what users would have done anyway, not whether the contact was correct.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: A6 defers protocol and seniority to humans, but the panel is labelled 'Recommended Contact' with a ranked list and no caveat. Users will treat it as authoritative, and fatigue sets in once the top suggestion proves wrong a few times. Staff then ignore it.

challenges.challenge_text: The stale badge will fire on a large share of contacts, because last_verified updates only when an Engagement is logged. In a CRM covering ~100 countries, many valid contacts (for example, a stable head of a ministry department with only occasional contact) will show 'stale' after 12 months, while departed officials with recent engagement show no badge. Once a large proportion of records carry the badge, staff will learn to ignore it, which is the alert-fatigue failure. The badge also never prompts action, since no verification workflow exists and no one owns the follow-up. It also does not account for our own coordinator turnover: when a Regional Coordinator leaves, their engagement logging stops and every contact they covered ages into stale together.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer treats the badge as an 'honest signal', but it is a noisy signal with no owner and no way to clear it except by logging an unrelated engagement. This is a solvable engineering gap, for example a lightweight one-click 'confirm still current' action or a 'left post' flag that removes the contact from ranking.

proposed_scope_in: Derived 'Suggested Contacts (activity-based)' panel on the Country record showing up to 3 contacts, with a 'Show all N contacts' link to the existing permission-filtered contact list. Ranking is a fixed, documented rule: (1) exclude contacts flagged inactive or whose Contact-Country link has a valid_to date in the past; (2) rank contacts linked to a Mission with status Active or a Project with status Open ahead of the rest; (3) most recent Engagement date, with contacts that have no engagement ranked last; (4) tie-break on primary_for_country, then alphabetical by name for stable ordering

Optional valid_from / valid_to date fields on the existing Contact-Country link (no new table, no new screen; they appear on the existing link edit form). A past valid_to removes the contact from ranking. The existing 'inactive' flag also removes them. Neither field is required

Each suggestion shows role/title, ministry, preferred channel, last engagement date (or 'no engagement recorded'), and a 'why shown' line. The panel carries a fixed caveat: 'Based on recorded activity, not verified current role or seniority. Confirm before sensitive correspondence.'
Optional boolean 'primary_for_country' on the existing Contact-Country link, which pins that contact to the top. Pinning does not override inactive or expired valid_to

'last_verified' is dropped as a concept. Replaced by a read-only, derived 'last engagement date', labelled as activity and not verification. A passive factual label 'No engagement in 12+ months' appears only on contacts shown in the top 3. There is no badge on list views and no verification workflow
Topic filter by Mission/Project via existing links only

'Who do I contact in [Country] for [Project/Mission]' from the Country page and global search. It runs live against the same permission-filtered query layer as the panel. It does not use a separate search index of contacts or justification strings

The 'why shown' line names a Mission, Project, or Engagement only if the user can read that record; otherwise it falls back to the generic text 'Linked to this country'. Engagement dates are shown only if the user can read the underlying Engagement

Contacts flagged inactive or with a past valid_to appear in 0 panel or query results (automated test)

Pilot validation: for 20 sampled countries across at least 5 regions, the owning Regional Coordinator reviews the top-3 list once (one-off pilot measurement, not a product workflow), and at least 70% of lists contain the correct current primary contact. Results are reported with the failure reasons (departed, junior-only, missing data) to inform v2

The 'No engagement in 12+ months' label appears on no more than 30% of top-3 suggestions in pilot data. A higher rate triggers a v2 review of the label

challenge_responses.response: The critique is right that engagement activity is not proof of current role, and that last_verified updated by engagement was misleading. Revisions that add no new tables, screens, or mandatory steps: (1) drop 'last_verified' and show a read-only, derived 'last engagement date' labelled as activity; (2) add optional valid_from/valid_to on the existing Contact-Country link, with a past valid_to excluding the contact from ranking; (3) the existing inactive flag excludes them deterministically; (4) a fixed caveat on the panel. I DEFEND not building cleanup, dedup, or turnover detection in v1: those need external data or manual programmes and would break the zero-friction goal. The ranking cannot know about a departure nobody records, and the caveat says so. A contact who has left is removed by one optional field edit on a record the coordinator is already viewing.

Valid concern, and the fix reuses the existing access model with no new screens, tables, or RBAC. (1) The panel, query, and global-search 'who do I contact' path run server-side through the existing permission-filtered queries, with no separate contact or justification search index, which removes the index-bypass path. (2) 'Why shown' text names a Mission, Project, or Engagement only if the user can read that record; otherwise it falls back to 'Linked to this country', so confidential Mission existence is not inferred. (3) Engagement dates show only if the underlying Engagement is readable. (4) A contact appears only if the user can see that Contact today. (5) The success criterion now explicitly tests the panel, query, search results and justification strings with differing-access users. The exact access rules for confidential Missions and what may be inferred are a security/classification decision that a human owner must confirm. I am implementing the existing rules, not defining new ones.

Ranking by seniority or decision-maker status needs a role/seniority taxonomy per country, protocol precedence rules, and manual maintenance by coordinators. That is policy content, not a product tweak, and it would break both schema simplicity and zero-entry. v1 labels the panel 'Suggested Contacts (activity-based)' and carries a caveat saying it reflects recorded activity, not seniority. The 'Show all N' link and optional primary_for_country pin let a human who knows the correct channel override the order. The critic's edge cases are handled by fixed documented rules without new scope: 'active' means Mission status Active or Project status Open (closed items do not boost ranking); ties break by primary_for_country and then alphabetically; contacts with no engagement rank last and show 'no engagement recorded'; more than 3 valid contacts show the top 3 plus the full list link. The weak survey metric is replaced by a coordinator-validated pilot on 20 sampled countries that measures correctness of the list and records failure reasons. Whether the junior-versus-decision-maker ranking should ever be automated is a diplomatic protocol question for humans, and I flag it for routing there.

A 'confirm still current' action or 'left post' flag would add a new UI action, a new manual coordinator step, and an ownership model for follow-up, which is exactly the data-entry friction that makes CRM data rot. The 'left post' need is already covered by the existing inactive flag and the optional valid_to from C1, so no new mechanism is required. Alert fatigue is mitigated by design: the label is passive, factual ('No engagement in 12+ months'), shown only on contacts in the displayed top 3 and never on list views, and success criteria cap its pilot incidence at 30% so fatigue is measured and not assumed. The critic's coordinator-turnover point is real but is a data-continuity issue; engagement logged by any user against the contact counts, not only the original coordinator's. Staffing and ownership of data verification are organisational decisions that sit outside this product scope.

challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision removes the misleading last_verified, adds optional valid_from/valid_to on the existing link, keeps the inactive flag, and adds a fixed 'not verified current role' caveat. The remaining risk of an unrecorded departure cannot be removed without external data or a workflow, and the caveat plus one-field exclusion bounds it acceptably for an MVP. The pilot will report 'departed' as a failure reason.

If these run over all records, the contact tied to Y moves to #1 and the user can infer that Y exists. The same applies to the 'Show all N' count and to the 'no engagement' placement. Only the display text is specified as permission-filtered.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Good on the index-bypass path (no separate index), the 'why shown' fallback text, engagement-date visibility, and the expanded UAT coverage. The proposal does not say that the ranking inputs (Mission/Project status boost, engagement recency, N) are computed only from records the requesting user can read. Please state that the rank, primary pin and counts are evaluated over the user-visible set, and add a UAT case where an unreadable Mission or Engagement must not change the order. This is a solvable engineering fix. Which Missions are confidential stays with the human owner.

It needs institutional policy sign-off on whether the panel may be used for sensitive correspondence.

assumptions.statement: Position changes are not detected automatically in v1. Turnover is handled by an optional valid_to or the inactive flag, and by a passive 'No engagement in 12+ months' label on top-3 contacts only.
assumptions.rationale: Auto-detection needs external data or workflows. Limiting the label to displayed top-3 contacts keeps it rare, and a plain factual label avoids implying verification.

assumptions.statement: Whether a person is appropriate for a sensitive topic, and seniority or protocol precedence, are diplomatic/policy judgments outside the CRM's remit and are escalated to a human policy owner.
assumptions.rationale: Keeping v1 to decision support avoids inventing policy and keeps scope small.

challenge_responses.response: Accepted: displayed-string filtering alone is not enough, since ranking and counts can leak the existence of a hidden Mission via order. The fix is a deterministic ordering change with no new screens, tables, RBAC, or coordinator steps. Permission filtering is now applied before ranking: the candidate contact set, the Mission/Project status boost, Engagement recency, the primary pin, the 'no engagement' placement, and N in 'Show all N' are all computed only from records the requesting user can read. A contact linked only to an unreadable Active Mission is ranked as if that link did not exist. No shared or cached global ranking is used, so there is no cross-user leakage path. I added a differential UAT case: changing hidden Missions, Projects, or Engagements must leave a restricted user's output byte-identical. Which Missions are confidential, and whether a visible contact linked to a confidential Mission should be shown at all, is a security/classification decision for a human owner. v1 implements existing access rules and does not define new ones.

challenges.challenge_text: Previously accepted: departed contacts are excluded via the inactive flag or valid_to, last_verified is dropped, and the panel carries an activity-only caveat.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Remains acceptable for an MVP. Not reopened.

challenges.challenge_text: The original risk: a coordinator who sees Country X but not a confidential Mission Y could infer Y's existence, or the contact linked to it, from ranking order, pin placement, the 'Show all N' count, or the 'why shown' text.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision closes the engineering gap. Permission filtering now runs before ranking, so the candidate set, status boost, recency, pin, 'no engagement' placement and N come only from records the user can read. There is no separate index and no cached shared ranking. 'Why shown' falls back to 'Linked to this country' when the record is unreadable. The automated differential test (byte-identical output when hidden Missions, Projects or Engagements change) and the UAT matrix with 5 users cover the panel, query, search, strings and count. Whether a visible contact linked to a confidential Mission should be shown at all is a classification decision, and the Proposer has left it to existing access rules. That is acceptable for an MVP.

challenges.challenge_text: Engagement recency is a poor proxy for seniority or decision-maker status. Ranking contacts for sensitive matters requires a protocol and seniority policy decision.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Already escalated to a human policy owner. The Proposer has explicitly kept seniority ranking out of scope. Stays escalated.

challenges.challenge_text: Previously accepted: the stale label is now limited to top-3 contacts, is passive and factual, and has a 30% review threshold, which bounds the risk of alert fatigue.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Acceptable for an MVP. Not reopened.

C1.challenge_text: Ranking by most recent Engagement date and active Mission linkage will surface people who have left their post. Example: a ministry liaison who attended three recent meetings resigns after a cabinet reshuffle. Nobody has logged a new engagement with the replacement, so the departed person stays ranked #1 with a fresh-looking 'why this person' justification. Staff then send sensitive correspondence to a former official. Because last_verified is only updated by logging an Engagement, it also marks a departed person as recently verified. It measures activity, not whether the person still holds the role. Also, no cleanup of inactive flags or duplicate contacts is planned, so data quality across 100 countries is unproven.

C2.challenge_text: Inheriting existing Country/Mission record-level access is not enough once contacts are aggregated into a derived panel, global search, and a 'who do I contact' query. Today a user may see a Country record without being able to browse its contacts, or may see a Mission without seeing every contact linked to it. A new ranked cross-record view, and the justification text (Mission/Project names, last engagement dates), can expose the existence of confidential missions or engagement history to staff who lack access to the underlying Mission or Engagement. Global search is the highest-risk path because it is often built on an index that bypasses record-level filters. A coordinator who can see Country X but not a confidential Mission Y could infer Y's existence and the named contact from the 'why this person' line. The 'zero instances in UAT' criterion cannot verify this unless it explicitly tests the derived panel, search index, and justification strings.

C3.challenge_text: The Proposer treats recency of engagement as a proxy for the 'right' contact. In practice the most-engaged contact is often a junior desk officer or an administrative assistant, while the decision-maker is engaged rarely. Rule (1) also lets any contact linked to an active Mission outrank everyone else, even if the link is stale (a Mission closed on paper but still marked active). A coordinator following the top-3 list for an urgent or sensitive matter reaches the wrong level and may bypass the correct ministry channel, a diplomatic misstep. There is also no handling of ties, contacts with no engagement history, or a country with more than three valid contacts. The 80% survey criterion is weak: it measures agreement with what users would have done anyway, not whether the contact was correct.

C4.challenge_text: The stale badge will fire on a large share of contacts, because last_verified updates only when an Engagement is logged. In a CRM covering ~100 countries, many valid contacts (for example, a stable head of a ministry department with only occasional contact) will show 'stale' after 12 months, while departed officials with recent engagement show no badge. Once a large proportion of records carry the badge, staff will learn to ignore it, which is the alert-fatigue failure. The badge also never prompts action, since no verification workflow exists and no one owns the follow-up. It also does not account for our own coordinator turnover: when a Regional Coordinator leaves, their engagement logging stops and every contact they covered ages into stale together.

final_decision.feature_request: We need a better way to track who is the right person to contact in each country.
final_decision.executive_summary: v1 adds a derived, activity-based 'Suggested Contacts' panel on the Country record. It shows up to 3 contacts ranked by a fixed, documented rule over existing Contact, Mission, Project and Engagement data. It also supports a 'who do I contact in [Country] for [Project/Mission]' query from the Country page and global search. Permission filtering is applied before ranking, so hidden records cannot affect order, pins or counts. The main trade-off argued was zero-friction, deterministic ranking from existing data versus the risk of surfacing departed, junior, or otherwise wrong contacts. This was bounded with optional valid_to/inactive exclusions, a fixed caveat, and a passive 12-month label, but seniority and protocol ranking were deliberately left out. A human policy owner must still decide whether activity-ranked suggestions may be used for sensitive correspondence (C3).
agreed_scope_included: Derived 'Suggested Contacts (activity-based)' panel on the Country record showing up to 3 contacts, with a 'Show all N contacts' link to the existing permission-filtered contact list

Fixed, documented ranking rule evaluated only over the user-visible set: (1) exclude contacts flagged inactive or whose Contact-Country link has a past valid_to; (2) rank contacts linked to an Active Mission or Open Project ahead of the rest, counting only records the user can read; (3) most recent readable Engagement date, with contacts with no visible engagement ranked last; (4) tie-break on primary_for_country, then alphabetical by name
Optional valid_from / valid_to date fields on the existing Contact-Country link (no new table, no new screen); a past valid_to or the existing inactive flag removes the contact from ranking

Each suggestion shows role/title, ministry, preferred channel, last engagement date (or 'no engagement recorded'), and a 'why shown' line, plus the fixed caveat 'Based on recorded activity, not verified current role or seniority. Confirm before sensitive correspondence.'
Optional boolean 'primary_for_country' on the existing Contact-Country link that pins a contact to the top among contacts the user can see; it does not override inactive or expired valid_to

'last_verified' dropped and replaced by a read-only derived 'last engagement date' (visible engagements only), labelled as activity and not verification; a passive 'No engagement in 12+ months' label appears only on top-3 contacts, with no badge on list views
Topic filter by Mission/Project via existing links only, applied only over Missions/Projects the user can read
'Who do I contact in [Country] for [Project/Mission]' from the Country page and global search, run live against the same permission-filtered query layer with no separate search index

Server-side permission enforcement applied BEFORE ranking: candidate set, status boost, engagement recency, primary pin, 'no engagement' placement and the count N are computed only from records the user can read; 'why shown' falls back to 'Linked to this country' for unreadable records
Confidential Missions/Engagements are defined by the existing access rules; v1 implements those and defines no new ones
agreed_scope_excluded: No new Contact, Role, or Relationship tables and no multi-table historical role graph
No verification workflow, 'confirm still current' task, approval chain, or follow-up ownership model in v1
No ML or tunable scoring model; no UI config screens for ranking rules or thresholds
No seniority, decision-maker, or protocol ranking (a diplomatic policy decision for humans, escalated under C3)
No custom RBAC, new permission model, sensitivity tiers, or field-level classification; existing Country/Mission access only
No bulk cleanup, dedup, or import of existing contact data; v1 uses data as it exists
No separate search index for contacts or derived justification text
No precomputed or cached global ranking shared across users; ranking is computed per request under the requesting user's permissions
No automated outreach, email/calendar integration, or external directory sync for detecting turnover

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Right person' means the best current point of contact for a country, optionally scoped by Mission or Project, not a single universal contact per country.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: No ledger issue targeted this assumption; it stood unchanged through all rounds.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Existing links and Engagement history are good enough to derive a useful suggestion. Departed contacts are excluded via the existing inactive flag or the new optional valid_to on the existing link, not via cleanup or detection.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C1 challenged this in R1; the Proposer revised it in R2 (dropped last_verified, added optional valid_to, added caveat) and the Critic accepted, noting residual risk from unrecorded departures is acceptable for an MVP.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Recency of engagement and active Mission/Project linkage are acceptable proxies for 'who is currently being dealt with' in v1, and the panel is decision support, not an authoritative routing engine.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C3 was defended by the Proposer in R2 (caveat, tie-break and no-engagement rules, 'Show all N', pin, coordinator-validated pilot) and escalated by the Critic because seniority/protocol precedence is a policy decision; it stayed escalated.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Users are Operations and Country Engagement staff. The panel, query, and justification text are computed server-side per request, with the existing Country/Mission/Engagement record-level permission filter applied to the candidate set and to every ranking input (status boost, recency, pin, count), and no separate index.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C2 was revised in R2 and again in R3 (permission filtering before ranking, differential leakage test); the Critic accepted in R3.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Position changes are not detected automatically in v1. Turnover is handled by an optional valid_to or the inactive flag, and by a passive 'No engagement in 12+ months' label on top-3 contacts only.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C4 was defended by the Proposer in R2 and accepted by the Critic as adequate for an MVP, given the passive label, top-3-only display, and the 30% pilot threshold.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Whether a person is appropriate for a sensitive topic, and seniority or protocol precedence, are diplomatic/policy judgments outside the CRM's remit and are escalated to a human policy owner.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: No ledger issue targeted this assumption directly; it was revised in R3 to reference the escalation, which relates to C3 under A3.

open_questions_for_humans: [C3] Policy owner for diplomatic protocol (e.g., Head of Diplomatic Security or Regional Director, with Legal as needed): may the activity-ranked 'Suggested Contacts' panel, which ranks by engagement recency and Mission/Project linkage and not by seniority or protocol precedence, be used for sensitive or urgent correspondence as-is with its caveat, and should any seniority/protocol precedence rule be defined for a later version? Until decided, v1 treats the panel as decision support only and includes no seniority ranking.
